messages.body_plain:
If you want to order the markers, then yes you would need to run orderMarkers.  formLinkageGroups() leaves the markers in an essentially arbitrary order, which would not be useful for QTL mapping.

The intensive parts are
  (a) using ripple() repeatedly
  (b) estimate the genetic map

You can speed up (a) by either skipping that part (use.ripple=FALSE) or using a different window size (window=2 or 3 rather than window=7).

You can speed up (b) by not running the algorithm to convergence (use maxit=6 rather than maxit=4000). You'd want to follow up with est.map() and replace.map(), so that the final map is estimated as well as possible.

I don't see anything wrong in your code that would give that error from write.cross.
What do you get when you type

  summary(All_q50C50trim)
  class(All_q50C50trim)

karl

messages.subject: Re: haploids; cM positions
messages.body_plain:
>
> 1) Can Rqtl be used with haploid data?
> Toxoplasma has a haploid genome so even though we know these are crosses they will never have heterozygous alleles. When I input them into my starting file I labeled them as AA and BB but when I gave them to R it insisted that the BB were all in fact AB
>
> toxo <- read.cross("csvr", file="/Users/Andrea/Documents/Lab Work/Rqtl/sortedSNPsearly.csv", genotypes =c("A", "B"), na.strings = "-", alleles =c("A", "B"))

Follow that with

  class(toxo)[1] <- "haploid"

or use crosstype="haploid" in the call to read.cross:

  toxo <- read.cross("csvr", file="/Users/Andrea/Documents/Lab Work/Rqtl/sortedSNPsearly.csv",
                     genotypes =c("A", "B"), na.strings = "-", alleles =c("A", "B"), crosstype="haploid")

> 2) Do I need to have marker ID's on my SNPs? None of them are named since they are just SNPs called from whole genome sequencing. Additionally, do the SNPs have to be in cM to work, I converted them but I would rather keep them in Mb (from bp) if that is cool with "qtl"

If you have very dense markers (very few recombination events between any two markers), it won't matter.

But if you have sufficient sample size, you can estimate the cM positions from the data:

  gmap <- est.map(toxo)
  toxo <- replace.map(toxo, gmap)

karl

But in the QTL analysis, pay attention to the fact that a given QTL may segregate in only a portion of the sibships: just as a marker might be homozygous in an F1 individual, so might the QTL.

I would get the estimated map using the combined sibships, jointly. And I would the same set of markers for everyone, just indicating NA in non-informative cases.

karl
